title: Triage handoff + SIEM field mapping (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for how vulnerability scanner outputs move from detection -> evidence enrichment -> SIEM export -> triage queue -> remediation tracking. Focus is on the handoff semantics, minimal SIEM field mapping we need for reliable alerts and forensic audit, and RBAC-v2 considerations for who can view/mark evidence as remediated. NOT final — iteration expected.

Scope:
- Vulnerability scanner findings across container images, repos, infra resources (k8s nodes, VMs, AMIs), and third-party deps.
- Events that should be exported to SIEM for detection correlation and audit.
- Handoff contract between scanner ingestion pipeline and Triage team backlog (including automation to create tickets).
- RBAC access constraints for evidence viewing and sensitive fields.

Background/context (why this matters):
- We currently have multiple scanner outputs (OSS SCA, container scanning, infra vuln scanners) landing in the evidence store with inconsistent metadata. That makes triage noisy and slows patch SLAs because triage can't correlate duplicates or find authoritative ownership.
- SIEM ingestion needs a stable, minimal fieldset to correlate across scanners and to support alerting rules (e.g., host_compromised + critical_vuln on same host).
- RBAC-v2 introduces resource-level grants; need to ensure evidence blobs containing PII/secret material are redacted for non-auditors.

Proposed minimal SIEM export schema (flat, required fields):
- event_type: "vuln_detection" | "vuln_update" | "remediation_state_change"
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- scanner_id: short id (e.g., "clair-2026-a")
- finding_id: stable dedup id (scanner_id:finding_hash)
- canonical_fingerprint: upstream dedupe key (sha256)
- severity: CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|INFO
- cvss_v3: numeric (optional if applicable)
- asset_type: container|host|repo|artifact|lambda
- asset_id: normalized asset identifier (aws://account/region/resource or k8s://cluster/namespace/pod)
- assigned_team: team id if auto-assigned (nullable)
- assigned_to: username (nullable)
- remediation_state: open|in_progress|fixed|wontfix|ignored
- patch_id: if applicable (e.g., GH PR number, kernel patch id)
- patch_sla_hours: numeric (int) — SLA target used at time of detection
- evidence_link: internal evidence store URL (short) — content access controlled by RBAC
- audit_hash: integrity hash of evidence snapshot (for later verification)
- correlator_id: used to group related findings across assets/events
- raw_severity_score: scanner-specific numeric score (optional)

Sample CSV-style export (fields above in header):
event_type,timestamp_utc,scanner_id,finding_id,canonical_fingerprint,severity,cvss_v3,asset_type,asset_id,assigned_team,assigned_to,remediation_state,patch_id,patch_sla_hours,evidence_link,audit_hash,correlator_id,raw_severity_score
vuln_detection,2027-02-10T08:12:33Z,sca-11,sca-11:7f3a9b,sha256:1a2b3c,CRITICAL,9.8,repo,github://redwood/ingest-service,eng-srv,alice@redwood.com,open,,72,https://evidence.redwood.internal/e/1,sha256:abc123,group-2027-02-10,98

RBAC-v2 notes (access + redaction):
- Role types relevant for this flow: vuln-reader, vuln-triager, vuln-admin, security-auditor.
- Principle: evidence_link may contain sensitive data (stack traces, sample payloads). Only vuln-triager and vuln-admin can fetch full evidence. vuln-reader gets a redacted view and metadata only. security-auditor role can access full evidence but access is logged separately and requires reason field in the audit.
- Access token life: evidence access tokens should be short-lived (max 15 minutes) and mutually authenticated between SIEM and internal evidence store.
- RBAC must be enforced at SIEM export level: SIEM should index the metadata fields above but not store full evidence blobs unless the SIEM instance is in a verified compliance zone. Otherwise, store evidence_link and audit_hash only.

Remediation tracking + patch SLA proposal (priority buckets + targets):
- P0 (exploitable, public exploit OR active compromise): SLA = 48 hours to remediation_state=in_progress, 7 days to fixed unless mitigation documented.
- P1 (critical with high likelihood): SLA = 72 hours to in_progress, 14 days to fixed.
- P2 (high/medium): SLA = 14 days to in_progress, 30 days to fixed.
- P3 (low/info): SLA = 90 days to review or closed as accepted risk.
Notes: patch_sla_hours exported in event should reflect the SLA at detection time and be used as input to ticket automation.

Triage handoff contract (scanner pipeline -> triage queue):
- On detection: pipeline emits vuln_detection event to message bus and writes normalized metadata to evidence store.
- Pipeline should attempt dedupe via canonical_fingerprint and correlator_id. If fingerprint matches open finding, emit vuln_update instead with merged evidence_link list.
- If severity >= HIGH, pipeline auto-creates a Jira ticket (project: SEC) and sets assigned_team via ownership map. Tickets include evidence_link and audit_hash and patch_sla_hours. JIRA keys should be included in linked_artifacts in the export.
- For medium/low, pipeline creates a triage task in backlog that triagers pull from via UI.

Automation hooks (examples):
- On vuln_update -> if evidence_count >= 3 and severity unchanged, auto-tag as "needs-priority-review" and ping triage Slack channel (#sec-triage).
- On remediation_state=fixed: pipeline writes remediation_state_change event and appends patch_id and proof_url. SIEM alert rule: if fixed==true and audit_hash verification fails, open an escalation ticket.

SIEM ingestion/alerting guidance:
- Index fields: finding_id, canonical_fingerprint, severity, asset_id, correlator_id, remediation_state, assigned_team, patch_sla_hours, timestamp_utc.
- Keep evidence_link out of long-term SIEM hot index; store in warm index for 30 days then cold (to reduce storage).
- Create watch for: (severity==CRITICAL && remediation_state!=fixed && hours_since_detection > patch_sla_hours) -> open paging alert routed to on-call sec responder.
- Correlation example: join vuln_detection with auth-success events on same host within 24h to raise an elevated incident.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Who owns the canonical_fingerprint algorithm? (Options: SCA team maintainers vs central evidence team)
- Do we want the SIEM to receive full evidence blobs for internal correlation (e.g., payload matching)? Compliance wants to avoid PII going to SIEM replicas outside compliance zones.
- How do we handle scanner upgrades that change raw_severity_score semantics? Need mapping version in export (scanner_schema_version).
- Should assigned_team be auto-derived from CODEOWNERS, or use a dedicated ownership service?

Action items (short):
- [Nina] Draft canonical_fingerprint proposal and post to confluence by 2027-02-18.
- [Jon] Prototype small CSV export and a SIEM ingestion config (runbook) by 2027-02-22. Reference repo: sec-infra/exporters.
- [Elena] Draft redaction rules for evidence (PII/stack traces) and RBAC policy text for vuln-reader vs triager by 2027-02-20.
- [Samir] Wire up auto-ticket creation POC for critical findings (JIRA project SEC) by 2027-02-25.

Notes to self / triage heuristics (working):
- If a finding has patch_id and patch_sla_hours <= 72 and assigned_team==null, escalate to platform-owners via oncall_roster lookup.
- Add correlator logic: cluster-level host drift events should join on host fingerprint + last 7 days.
- Keep the SIEM field names short and snake_case to ease mapping across different SIEM vendors.

References & links:
- Confluence: SEC-Triage-Handoff-Overview (linked above)
- JIRA: SEC-1023 (ownership mapping), SEC-1107 (ticket automation backlog)
- GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sec-infra/pull/87 (exporter prototype)

This doc is intentionally conversational; we should convert to a formal runbook once decisions are made on canonical_fingerprint and RBAC redaction rules.

-- end of draft --
